title: statespace specimen, version 1
description: A specimen: a counterexample kept beside its fix, with a label that is generated from the run that found it (spine section 5.1; DESIGN.md section 6.5). A course specimen is a record in content/specimens/ (SP-1.1 to SP-1.10 in W1); a learner's own specimen is a record in specimens/ of the lab repository (ARCHITECTURE.md section 8.2), whose ID is minted when it is mounted. The record holds what a run cannot say: the title, the property it violates, the cause, the class, the fix, the KC tags, and where in the course it is found. It holds pointers to what a run can say: the runs and the queries in them. It holds no witness, no stamp, no engine version, no date and no status, so no label can be typed: the witness, the stamp, the tool version, the date and whether the witness is minimal are read from the cited runs, and the status (mounted, then kept after a re-find on a fresh variant at least 7 days later) is derived from the learner's events at read time (I2). A field that is not listed here is an error, which is how a stamp, a tool version or a stored status typed into a record is refused. This schema checks the shape; the label builder and the cabinet's checks also confirm that every pointer names a verdict line that the run holds, that each witness replays, and that a minimal claim rests on an Optimize query or an unsat core.

id.description: SP-n.k for a course specimen, which the ID registry (generated from the spine) holds; a learner's specimen has an ID minted when it is mounted, never typed, and not of the form SP-n.k. At most 64 characters.

title.description: What the specimen is called on its label: a short name, one line. For a course specimen it is words of the spine's table (section 5.1).

draft.description: True while the record is unreviewed: the cabinet then says "Draft: first-learner pass pending." Absent means false.

kcs.description: The knowledge components the specimen teaches, the primary one first. Every specimen carries KC tags (spine section 4; GATE-kc).

found_in.description: Where in the course the specimen is found: the lesson of the spine's table (section 5.1), or, for a learner's own specimen, the lab stage whose check found it.

mount.description: How a course specimen comes to be mounted for a learner: at the learner's first call on a cell of one of these lessons (a call event whose ref is call:S{n}.L{k}/{cell}). Absent for a learner's own specimen.

violates.description: The property the witness violates, as one line (the label's Violates row). For a specimen about a verdict, what the verdict does not establish.

because.description: The cause, as one line (the label's Because row).

class.description: The class of witness it belongs to, in words (the label's Class row; M-class-hint), as the generators that serve a re-find name it.

cured_by.description: The fix (the label's Cured by row), linked to the claim it mints.

evidence.description: The runs the label is generated from.

incident.description: Present when the specimen is a dated incident, kept as a toy model (SP-1.9, SP-1.10, SP-4.5, SP-5.7, SP-6.11 and SP-8.5; spine section 12 item 16): the date, the source, and that the model is a toy. Never exploit code.

title.description: A title: 1 to 120 characters and no line break.

text.description: One line of learner copy: 1 to 300 characters and no line break. {{run:RUN-id}} stands for a run chip; a value reference ({{run:RUN-id#values.name}}) is not used here, because the label reads values from the cited lines.

kcId.description: A knowledge component, such as KC-1.violation-as-sat.

query.description: The name of a query in a run: the label of its verdict line, `[variant_violation] sat ...` or `rlimit-case unknown ...`, without the brackets. The run's lines hold exactly one verdict line of that name.

foundIn.description: Where the specimen is found: a lesson, a lab stage, or both.

mount.description: The lessons whose first call mounts the specimen: the earliest call event on a cell of any of them, by an unassisted or assisted learner and never an agent, is the instant it was mounted.

curedBy.description: The fix, in words, with the claim it mints and, for a lab specimen, the file in fixed/ that holds it.

claim.description: The claim template whose card the fix mints, such as CL-1.1.

fixed.description: The fixed version, kept beside the broken one: a path in the lab repository.

evidence.description: The runs behind the label: the main query, whose verdict line gives the witness (or the raw answer) and the stamp; further queries shown beside it; and how the witness was minimized, if it was.

also.description: Further queries the label shows beneath the main one, each with its caption: a second witness, the violation query beside a premise query.

main.description: The query the stamp is read from. A solver's sat or unsat means opposite things for a violation query and a premise query (DESIGN.md section 5.4), and a run's lines do not say which it is, so the record does.

direction.description: What the query asserts: a violation of the property (a sat is then a counterexample), or the premises alone (an unsat is then a sign that they contradict each other).

steps.description: The witness's length in steps, when it is not one transfer: a witness of two captures is 2. Absent means 1.

premise.description: The premise query that sits beside a violation query's unsat: the label reads its verdict, and an unsat there means the claim holds vacuously.

replay.description: Where the witness was replayed when the main query's own lines do not say it (a replay line beginning "replay ok"): a query of another run whose line replays this very witness.

also.description: A further query the label shows, with a caption in one line. A sat that the label shows must replay, as the main one must: replay names the query of another run whose line replays it, when the query's own lines do not.

minimal.description: Whether the witness is minimal, per engine (DESIGN.md section 6.5): for Z3, only under an explicit Optimize objective (optimize) or as an unsat core whose members are each needed (core); none says it was not minimized; not-applicable says the question does not arise, as for a verdict.

objective.description: For optimize: the variable or quantity the Optimize query minimizes, whose value the label prints.

confirm.description: For optimize: a plain query of the same run that asks for anything below the minimum and answers unsat, the check that the minimum is one.

why.description: For not-applicable: why the question does not arise.

incident.description: A dated incident kept as a toy model: the day it was found or published, its source, and that the model is a toy of it. The source is a public page, named and linked.

toy_model.description: True: the run is a model of the incident's mechanism, not the incident's code.

incidentSource.description: A public source: its title and its https address.
